questions.q: Reading glasses are made from which type of lenses?

Without corrective spectacles, they find it difficult to see nearby objects clearly and comfortably. This defect is called presbyopia. Later, it was found that many elements and compounds behave similarly at low temperatures. Such substances are called superconductors. Since superconductors show no resistance, there is no loss of energy when current flows through them. Therefore, superconductors can be used efficiently for transmitting electricity from one place to another. Another essential property of superconductors is that they prevent magnetic flux from entering their interior The magnetic field/flux is confined to the surface, i.e., their magnetic permeability is zero.

questions.explanation: ‘Manav’ is India’s first indigenous 3D (three-dimensional) printed humanoid robot. Manav is a two-foot-tall humanoid robot and looks like a big toy. It has 21 sensors. There are two cameras in its eye sockets and two microphones on both sides of its head. This robot, made by Diwakar Vaish, was unveiled at IIT Bombay Techfest 2014–2015.

questions.q: What is true of the GSLV-F15 mission by ISRO?
questions.question_type: Correct Statement — Single Correct

options.B: It marked ISRO's 101st launch from Sriharikota
options.C: It marked ISRO's 100th launch from Sriharikota
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: On 29 January 2025, ISRO launched GSLV-F15 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, as the 100th launch mission from Sriharikota. Through this launch vehicle, the NVS-02 navigation satellite for the NavIC system was placed into a Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO). The launch and satellite injection into GTO were successful; however, during the later orbit-raising process, the oxidizer valve did not open. Therefore, the satellite could not reach the intended geosynchronous orbit and remained in an elliptical orbit. Now it is not operational. Since both options (a) and (c) are correct, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.q: The name of the lander, a part of the Chandrayaan-2 spacecraft recently launched by India, is -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: It was launched on 22 July 2019 by GSLV Mk III-M1 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota (Andhra Pradesh). The name of its lander is Vikram. Chandrayaan-3 was launched on 14 July 2023 by GSLV Mk III (LVM3-M4) from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota (Andhra Pradesh).

questions.q: Satellites are used for-
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Satellites are used in many different fields, including communication, broadcasting, and meteorology. An artificial satellite is an electronic device sent for a specific purpose, which orbits the Earth or any other celestial body, whereas a natural satellite is a celestial body in space that revolves around a planet.

questions.q: When was Insat-2A launched?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: INSAT-2A was launched on 10 July 1992 from French Guiana.

questions.q: Who was the inventor of Radar?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Scottish physicist Robert Watson developed the first experimental radar (RADAR—Radio Detection and Ranging) system in 1935. During World War II, this system was used to give warning before air attacks.

questions.q: Sir C.V. Raman received Nobel Prize for physics in the year :
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Dr. Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Physics. He received this award in 1930.

questions.q: Raman effect is due to Sir C.V. Raman. Which of the following statements is correct about the 'Raman effect'?
questions.question_type: Correct Statement — Single Correct

options.A: The Raman effect is an example of elastic scattering of light.
options.B: The frequency of scattered light increases and decreases after scattering.

questions.q: Einstein got the Nobel Prize for :
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Albert Einstein was honoured for his services to theoretical physics, especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for 1921, and he received the prize in 1922.

questions.q: Name the scientist who said that matter can be converted into energy—
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Einstein explained that mass and energy are not two separate forms; they can be converted into each other. In this context, he established a relation between mass and energy, known as Einstein’s mass–energy equation. According to this, mass (matter) can be converted into energy, and energy can again be converted into mass. E = mc²; Where E is energy, m is mass, and c is the speed of light.

questions.q: Who was the scientist who discovered the telescope?

questions.q: Which of the following statements are true about Akashteer?
questions.question_type: Correct Statement — Single Correct

options.A: Akashteer is the core of the Indian Army’s air defence system.
options.B: It integrates seamlessly with India’s wider C4ISR system.
options.C: It reflects a strategic shift from passive defence to active and rapid counter-action.
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Akashteer is the main command-and-control system of the Army’s air defence setup, through which different air defence units, radars, and weapon systems are connected as a network. It functions in integration with India’s larger C4ISR (Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance) ecosystem and enables coordinated working among the three services. It automatically monitors the low-altitude airspace and efficiently controls ground-based air defence weapon systems, thereby shifting India’s strategy from passive defence to active and rapid counter-action. Therefore, option (d) is correct.

questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A barometer is an instrument that measures atmospheric pressure and helps in weather forecasting. A sudden rise in the barometer reading indicates extremely dry weather, whereas a sudden fall indicates stormy conditions. A gradual fall in the barometer reading suggests the possibility of rainfall.

questions.q: Quartz crystals used in clocks are :
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Quartz crystals used in watches are silicon dioxide (SiO2). In nature, some forms are found as rock crystal and rhinestone. However, those used commercially are generally manmade. Quartz crystals are also used in radio and television.

questions.q: Which of the following is the value of the solar constant ?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The solar constant is the amount of solar energy received per second per unit area at the upper boundary of the Earth’s atmosphere. It is also defined as the flux density of solar radiation. It is not a truly constant value, because it can vary with time. According to NASA, the solar constant is about 1.361 kW/m², and it keeps varying between 1.360 and 1.367 kW/m². Therefore, the nearest option (b) is correct.

questions.explanation: The Higgs boson is a fundamental particle. It was first proposed in 1964, and its experimental confirmation was achieved on 14 March 2013. questions.q: Which of the following is a non-contact force ?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Magnetic force is an example of a non-contact force, whereas frictional force and impact force are examples of contact forces. In non-contact forces, objects are unlikely to come into direct contact with each other.

questions.q: In 2012, a highly publicized 'God particle' was discovered at the CERN European Laboratory. The scientific name of this particle is:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: In 2012, through experiments at the Large Hadron Collider in the CERN European Laboratory, the ‘Higgs boson’, popularly called the ‘God particle’, was discovered. This hypothesis was presented in 1964 by Nobel Prize–winning scientist Peter Higgs. The particle was named the Higgs boson after Higgs and the Indian scientist Satyendra Nath Bose.

questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: A photovoltaic cell is generally called a solar cell. It is a non-mechanical device that converts sunlight directly into electricity, whereas a photodiode is a detector of light signals. Therefore, for digital applications (switching/controlling), a photodiode is used. It is notable that solar light is made up of photons. questions.q: The credit for research and development in space science goes to—
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: In India, the main source of inspiration for research and development in space science was the renowned space scientist Dr. Vikram Sarabhai. Dr. V. questions.q: The father of the Indian program in atomic energy is—
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha is the father of the Indian atomic energy program. In India, on 10 August 1948, the Atomic Energy Commission was constituted under the chairmanship of Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha.

questions.q: In using nuclear power for peaceful purposes, India is far ahead of which country?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Pakistan, which conducted nuclear tests following India's nuclear tests. However, Pakistan’s nuclear program is focused on developing nuclear weapons, whereas the main objective of India’s nuclear program is its peaceful use through nuclear power generation. India passed the Atomic Energy Act in 1948 and clearly declared that nuclear research would be used for peaceful progress. In terms of nuclear power generation and other nuclear applications that improve human life (such as medical uses, food preservation, etc.), India is far ahead of Pakistan.

questions.q: The name of the tank manufactured in India is—
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Among the given options, the tank manufactured in India is Arjun. questions.q: When was the first Indian satellite Aryabhata launched?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: India’s first satellite ‘Aryabhata’ was launched on 19 April 1975 from Kapustin Yar using the Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket. The satellite was named after the ancient Indian mathematician Aryabhata.
